agentAccessAgentPromptRemote.message:
Use Agent Access to request vault credentials once you've been paired with it.

Pairing isn't something to do from this conversation: the person running you already has, or will generate, a one-time pairing token and runs $CLI$ connect --token <token> themselves, directly on this machine. Don't ask for that token or offer to run the pairing command with it — it's a vault-access credential and must never be pasted into a prompt.

Once paired, to log in or authenticate with a saved credential, run:
$CLI$ run --domain <domain> -- <command>

The credential is injected into <command>'s environment (AAC_USERNAME, AAC_PASSWORD, AAC_TOTP, etc.) and scrubbed from anything it prints, so you never see the actual username, password, or TOTP code.

To look up an item without using it, run:
$CLI$ get --domain <domain>

This returns a reference (bw://item/<id>) and the item's name, never the secret values.

To act on a specific item you already have a reference for, run:
$CLI$ run --ref bw://item/<id> -- <command>

Each request opens an approval prompt on the paired computer. A human there has to be present to approve it, so this doesn't work unattended.
